ca_castle_rock_loop.blurb: Boulders strung along the main loop trail in the Castle Rock State Park area of the San Francisco Bay Area. The rock is sandstone, and it is fragile and easily damaged when wet, so dry conditions matter here. This is bouldering only, with a wide spread: plenty of V0 to V4 problems, a middle band around V5 to V7, and a handful of hard ones that reach V10 and V12. Magoos is the biggest cluster, and Parking Lot Rock, 360 Degree Boulder and Eco Terrorist Boulder hold much of the rest. Problems include traverses, roofs, an arete and sit starts, spread over many separate boulders rather than one big wall.

co_sand_gulch.blurb: A small canyon area within Shelf Road, near Canon City, Colorado. Shelf Road is limestone, flaky and pocketed in places, and here the best lines follow long vertical faces threaded with pockets, cracks and horizontal seams. Two walls, Contest Wall and Free Form Wall, hold nearly all of the climbing, with Sand Gulch Bouldering and Dead Colt Canyon adding a few more. Sport routes dominate, with a few trad leads and a handful of boulder problems. Grades run from about 5.8 to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11 and relatively few easier lines. The cliffs face different directions, so sun or shade can usually be found at any hour.

il_fountain_bluff_land_water_reserve.blurb: A bluff in far southern Illinois overlooking the Mississippi River. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a trad minority and a few boulder problems, and a number of the lines are multi-pitch. Grades range from 5.6 to 5.13, but most sit between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits stronger climbers best. The walls include steep faces, slabs and roof pulls, and The Big Wall towers over its surroundings. Other sectors include The Gendarme Area, Fountain Bluff East, Waterfall East and Waterfall West, each holding a dozen or more climbs.

qc_trois_rives.blurb: A forested cliff site in the Mauricie region of Quebec, beside the Saint-Maurice River and roughly an hour and a half by road from Trois-Rivieres. Trad is the main style, with a good number of sport routes, some top-rope climbs and a small set of boulders. Grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.11, with some easier lines and a few at 5.12 and above. Etoile holds the most climbs, alongside Gauche, L'aiguille and Droite for trad, Ecole for top-roping, and Panoramique and Coin sportif for bolted climbing.

qc_weir.blurb: A cliff on Mont Larose in the Laurentians of Quebec, near Montcalm, rising about 100 metres beside a cluster of satellite dishes. The climbing is varied: slabs, faces, overhangs, roofs, dihedrals and cracks, with single-pitch routes and two or three pitch lines, plus a little aid. Sport and trad are roughly even, with a few top ropes. Grades run mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with some 5.13 and a smaller number of easier lines. The cliff was long seen as short on easy climbs, but rebolting and new routes have since added options across many grades. Sections include Mur de l'Ouest, Black and White, Ligne jaune and Mur du Capitaine.
